# RealIRacing

> RealIRacing (realiracing.com) is an iRacing sim racing site by Carlos Martinez: practical guides on force feedback settings, wheel and pedal buyer's guides, safety rating and racecraft, car and track guides, and OBS streaming setups, plus race highlights, setup guides and rig tours on the @realtape YouTube channel. Real motorsport roots, tested on a real rig.

## About
- Author: Carlos Martinez (iRacing user "Carlos Martinez9"). Home: https://realiracing.com/
- Rig: MOZA R9 direct drive wheelbase, MOZA CS V2 wheel, MOZA CRP2 load cell pedals, RTX 5060 Ti, 1440p 120 Hz monitor. Full breakdown: https://realiracing.com/gear.html
- Affiliate disclosure: gear links go to Amazon and carry an affiliate tag; the author may earn a commission at no cost to the reader. The site does not use sponsored loaner hardware.
- 165 blog guides published so far; new posts appear several times a week.

## Main sections
- [Home](https://realiracing.com/): channel overview, content types, gear picks, FAQ
- [Blog](https://realiracing.com/blog/): all iRacing guides, settings and gear advice
- [My Rig](https://realiracing.com/gear.html): every part Carlos races and streams on, with notes on why
- [Link hub](https://realiracing.com/go/): all platforms in one place
- [YouTube @realtape](https://www.youtube.com/@realtape): race highlights, setup guides, rig tours, iRacing tips
- Social: [Instagram @realiracing](https://www.instagram.com/realiracing) · [TikTok @realiracing](https://www.tiktok.com/@realiracing) · [X @realiracing](https://x.com/realiracing)

## Latest blog posts (newest first)

- [A 45-Minute iRacing Practice Plan That Actually Sticks](https://realiracing.com/blog/iracing-practice-session-plan-45-minutes.html): A structured 45-minute iRacing practice session: warm-up, one corner and one variable, a consistent run, a pace run, lap review and a firm stop.
- [Laguna Seca iRacing Guide: The Corkscrew and Where to Brake](https://realiracing.com/blog/laguna-seca-iracing-guide-corkscrew-braking.html): A first-person guide to WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca on iRacing: how to learn the blind crests, brake into the Corkscrew and tune force feedback.
- [The 15-Minute Monthly Check for a Fixed Sim Rig](https://realiracing.com/blog/sim-rig-monthly-check-bolts-pedals-quick-release.html): Loose bolts mimic bad force feedback and pedal drift. My monthly rig check for the frame, wheelbase, quick release, pedals and seat.
- [Sim Racing in an Apartment: Noise, Vibration and Neighbours](https://realiracing.com/blog/sim-racing-in-an-apartment-noise-vibration-neighbours.html): Where a sim rig's noise really comes from, what travels through floors, and the fixes that kept my direct drive rig neighbour-friendly.
- [Bass Shakers and Tactile Feedback: Real Benefit or Expensive Gimmick?](https://realiracing.com/blog/bass-shakers-tactile-feedback-worth-it.html): I tested bass shakers on my MOZA rig. Here's whether the money actually improves your lap times or just your immersion.
- [Indianapolis Motor Speedway Oval: Trim, Drafting, and Speed](https://realiracing.com/blog/indianapolis-motor-speedway-oval-drafting-trim.html): Master Indy's high-speed oval with proper trim setup and drafting technique. Real lap data and MOZA R9 feedback insights for consistent top-10 pace.
- [Dirt Late Model iRacing Guide: Setup, Technique, and Racecraft](https://realiracing.com/blog/dirt-late-model-iracing-guide.html): Master dirt late model racing on iRacing. Learn setup fundamentals, throttle control, and how to race clean on unpredictable surfaces.
- [Homestead Miami Speedway iRacing Guide: Setup and Racing Line](https://realiracing.com/blog/homestead-miami-iracing-oval-guide.html): Master Homestead's tight oval layout with FFB tuning, brake zones, and passing strategy on my MOZA R9 rig.
- [Bristol Motor Speedway iRacing Guide: Setup, Line, Strategy](https://realiracing.com/blog/bristol-motor-speedway-iracing-guide.html): Master Bristol's tight half-mile banking with proven setup tuning, throttle control, and fuel strategy tips for consistent iRacing oval racing.
- [Imola iRacing Guide: Kerbs, Chicanes, and Late Braking Zones](https://realiracing.com/blog/imola-iracing-guide-kerbs-chicanes-strategy.html): Master Imola's technical layout with specific braking points, kerb-riding lines, and chicane entry strategies. Real-world line analysis for consistent lap times.
- [Time Trials and Time Attack: Racing Against Yourself in iRacing](https://realiracing.com/blog/time-trials-time-attack-racing-yourself.html): Master the mental discipline and technical consistency needed to excel in time trials. Learn how to build pace lap-by-lap without traffic interference.
- [Used Sim Racing Wheelbase: What to Check Before Buying](https://realiracing.com/blog/used-sim-racing-wheelbase-inspection-guide.html): Inspect motor health, firmware compatibility, and wear patterns before buying a used direct-drive wheelbase. Avoid dead units and costly repairs.
- [Why a Fast Setup Can Actually Make You Slower in iRacing](https://realiracing.com/blog/fast-setup-makes-you-slower-iracing.html): A setup optimized for raw pace can punish mistakes and hurt consistency. Learn why baseline trumps edge-case performance.
- [Understanding Strength of Field in iRacing: What SOF Really Means](https://realiracing.com/blog/strength-of-field-iracing-explained.html): Strength of Field (SOF) determines your iRacing incident and safety rating gains. Learn how it's calculated and why racing weak fields costs you more mistakes.
- [Meta Quest 3 VR vs Triple Monitors for iRacing: Which to Buy First](https://realiracing.com/blog/meta-quest-3-vr-vs-triple-monitors-iracing-buying-guide.html): Weighing the real cost, immersion, and practical downsides of Meta Quest 3 VR versus a triple-monitor setup for iRacing, here is what I would recommend based on your budget.
- [MOZA SR-P vs Fanatec CSL Pedals LC: Budget Load-Cell Pedals Compared](https://realiracing.com/blog/moza-sr-p-vs-fanatec-csl-pedals-lc-budget-load-cell.html): Both bring load-cell braking under ~$200. Here's how the MOZA SR-P and Fanatec CSL Pedals LC actually compare for consistent, repeatable braking in iRacing.
- [Fanatec ClubSport DD vs MOZA R12: Which High-End Direct Drive to Buy](https://realiracing.com/blog/fanatec-clubsport-dd-vs-moza-r12-buying-guide.html): Comparing two of the strongest mid-to-high torque direct-drive wheelbases on price, ecosystem, and real FFB feel for iRacing.
- [Logitech G923 vs Thrustmaster T300: Which Should Be Your First Wheel](https://realiracing.com/blog/logitech-g923-vs-thrustmaster-t300-first-wheel.html): Comparing the two most common entry wheels for iRacing beginners: belt versus gear drive, pedal sets, and which one actually holds up as you improve.
- [Fuji Speedway iRacing Guide: Lines, Setup, Wet Weather](https://realiracing.com/blog/fuji-speedway-iracing-guide.html): Master Fuji's fast uphill corners and technical downhill sections. Learn racing lines, brake points, and setup tweaks for both wet and dry conditions.
- [Indianapolis Motor Speedway iRacing Guide: Line, Setup, Drafting](https://realiracing.com/blog/indianapolis-motor-speedway-iracing-guide.html): Master Indy's high-speed oval. Learn the racing line, brake zones, setup priorities, and drafting strategy for clean, competitive lap times.
